events.body:
## Outcome

Developers can use ForkMesh repositories through normal Git commands and existing clients without a ForkMesh-specific source-control dialect.

## Scope

- Cover clone, fetch, push, hooks, branches, rebase, force-with-lease and force updates, shallow and partial clones, bundles, submodules, and signed commits.
- Test common terminal versions and desktop clients against direct, relay, and mirror-failover paths.
- Define safe, actionable failures wherever a capability is intentionally unsupported.

## Acceptance criteria

- The versioned conformance suite exercises every promised operation and detects ref or object corruption.
- Supported stock clients require no custom patch and preserve signatures and object IDs.
- Known limitations are generated into the public matrix with reproductions and last-tested versions.
- Linked automated evidence covers supported platforms, failure paths, rollback/recovery, documentation, and telemetry before closure.

## Delivery and dependencies

- Portfolio tier: **P0 release gate**
- Milestone: **Preservation public alpha**
- Numeric priority: **5 of 44** (1 is highest)
- Depends on: None
- Assignee: unassigned until an accountable owner accepts the epic; fund independently releasable child issues rather than this umbrella epic.

## Progress baseline

**50% as of 2026-07-22.** Clone, fetch, mirroring, browsing, release artifacts, and owner push foundations exist; the complete cross-client matrix and edge cases remain. Progress may not exceed 85% without end-to-end validation or 95% without security, documentation, telemetry, and rollout evidence.

## Verification and measures

Primary measures: Compatibility pass rate by operation/client/transport and zero data-loss regressions. Closure requires linked test runs, operational evidence, and current user-facing documentation.
events.title: Preserve standard Git workflow compatibility
